findings.claim: LEDGER's revision resolver needed no fence of its own; composed with H6's never-raise contract it needs one, and neither leg could see that. _resolve_revision only reads files, so LEDGER never wrapped its call site. H6's moneta_provenance() carries a hard contract — _make_store calls it from inside its own except handler, so a raise there escapes _make_store and stops Houdini's panel loading. The naive union puts an unfenced resolver inside a function contracted never to raise.

findings.claim: The composition put an uncached, stage-opening probe onto a per-record caller. ledger._deposit_to_moneta calls moneta_provenance() once per deposit, and backfill() once per parsed record. Post-union that call also runs _schema_registered_detail() — uncached BY DESIGN (R64 item 4: a cache could not observe a subprocess setting PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME, which is the only honest way to test it) — and _schema_in_use_detail(), which opens and traverses a USD stage of up to 20,000 prims when a root is resolved. The ledger seam reads only file/version/revision from the payload; it never reads the schema fields it now pays for.
findings.severity_reasoning: LATENT, not live. With $SYNAPSE_MONETA_USD_ROOT unset — the documented default, 'Both: leave unset unless pointing the doctor at a real stage' — _resolve_usd_root returns immediately and the cost is zero disk I/O. The registry query is a singleton dict lookup. The cost only materialises for an operator who has deliberately pointed the doctor at a stage and then runs a backfill.
findings.fix: Added probe_schema=False as a keyword-only opt-out with its own reason constant. The ledger call site is deliberately UNCHANGED — see U1-FR-1.

for_ruling.detail: U1-F2. The ledger seam reads only file/version/revision from the provenance payload and never reads schema_registered or schema_in_use, but post-union it pays for them once per deposited record. The opt-out exists and is pinned; the call site is unchanged. Three things would have to move together: the call site itself, the committed mutation anchor `provenance-only-on-success` (which matches that exact source line), and four test stubs that monkeypatch moneta_provenance with a zero-argument function. All three are mechanical.
for_ruling.ask: Rule whether the per-record path opts out. If yes, U1 or a follow-on makes all three edits atomically. If no, U1-F2 stands as an accepted, documented cost.
for_ruling.agent_position: Did not act. This is cost versus diagnostic completeness — a defensible-either-way judgement, which Article I sends here rather than to my own discretion. The default posture ($SYNAPSE_MONETA_USD_ROOT unset) makes the cost zero today, so nothing is urgent, and changing three files to save nothing measurable in the shipped configuration is the kind of change that should be ruled rather than assumed.

for_ruling.topic: probe_schema is an addition neither leg nor any ruling specified
for_ruling.detail: R64 named five fields. probe_schema is a sixth thing — a parameter — introduced because the composition created a cost neither leg could see (U1-F2). It is purely additive: the default is True, every existing caller is unchanged, and the opted-out state is a distinct reason string rather than a fourth way of saying False. It carries four pins and four mutations.
for_ruling.ask: Keep or strike. If struck, moneta_provenance() reverts to (usd_root=None) and U1-F2 becomes an open, unmitigated item rather than a mitigated one.
for_ruling.agent_position: Recommend keep, but flagging it because scope discipline matters more than my preference. The brief said 'preserve every constraint both legs established', not 'add API', and I would rather have this struck by a ruling than have it survive because nobody noticed it was unasked-for.

for_ruling.topic: H6's reader controls (M3, M4) remain unreproducible
for_ruling.detail: U1-F4 residual. H6's two R60 reader controls — 'the reader reads the root layer instead of composing sublayers' and 'any prim counts as a match' — are the highest-value mutations in its battery and the only ones that could catch a blind reader. They live only in H6.json as prose. They are not single-line edits, so U1 did not re-materialise them rather than materialise them badly.
for_ruling.ask: Whether a follow-on materialises H6's M3/M4 into the committed battery. Related to R80's ordered-but-absent checks: the general rule this suggests is that a leg's mutation battery must be COMMITTED, not scratch, or its result is inherited the moment the file it measures changes.
for_ruling.agent_position: Evidence, not a decision. The specific risk is bounded — _schema_in_use_detail was copied byte-for-byte and its pins pass — but 'copied verbatim' is strictly weaker than 'the mutation still fires', and I would rather say so than let 39/39 imply otherwise.
